what: Recorded package-manager readings for the M-Import import core (tests/host_import_core.rs) and its configuration capture (tests/host_import_files.rs).
written_by: a person, from public package metadata: the shapes dpkg-query -W, dpkg-query -W -f=${Conffiles}, apt-cache policy, apt-mark show..., pacman -Q/-Qe/-Qi/-Qii/-Qqem and pacman -Si print. No machine was read to produce them.
not_captured_from_this_machine: AGENTS.md section 8 forbids reading this machine's package database or /etc as test input, and this machine has no package manager the host scope can drive. Nothing here was captured, copied or derived from it.
no_personal_data: No user name, no host name, no home path, no address and no real machine identity appears in any file below this one. The package names, versions and sections are public distribution metadata; the deliberately unavailable names (lodi-hand-built, ubuntu-hand-built) and the off-base scenarios' lodi-agent, lodi-tool and tela-icon-theme are invented for the test and exist in no repository. The source addresses in the apt recordings are the public distribution, Docker and Launchpad ones the shapes carry, and no address reaches an emitted file. The configuration files under the capture scenarios are short invented texts, and the one that carries a private-key marker carries the marker line alone and no key.

scenarios.fresh: Models a machine straight from that distribution's own installer, not a cloud or container image: the base system, its metapackages, and nothing a person chose.
scenarios.chosen: The same machine after a person installed a handful of things, including one name whose installed version the local package database alone knows and, on Arch, one foreign (AUR) build.
scenarios.capture: The chosen machine plus a conffiles recording: two files the package manager reports as changed, one it reports unchanged, and the files under etc/ they name.
scenarios.refusals: The chosen machine plus a conffiles recording naming one file of every class the capture refuses — outside /etc, on the hard path list, not a plain file, unreadable to all, too large, not text, a private-key marker — so that each refusal is proved by name.
scenarios.credentials: The chosen machine plus a conffiles recording of sixteen changed files under /etc/credential-shapes/, one per credential shape of tests/support/credentials.rs, and one benign file. The tests write each file's bytes themselves: every value in them is invented and grants nothing, and each file is refused by the content scan while the benign one is captured (LD-335).
scenarios.capture-many: The chosen machine plus a conffiles recording of thirty changed files, enough that the bundle reaches its 1 MiB cap and the rest are refused.
scenarios.multiarch: The evidence shape of LD-305, on apt: a machine whose Multi-Arch libraries dpkg-query qualifies by architecture while apt-mark prints them plain. It records BOTH answers dpkg-query gives -- dpkg-query.txt and dpkg-survey.txt are what ${Package} prints, dpkg-query-binary.txt and dpkg-survey-binary.txt what ${binary:Package} prints -- and the test's shim replays whichever the product's own format string asks for, so the recording proves which identity the installed set is read under. Fourteen names are qualified; thirteen are automatic, and the fourteenth is a library a person chose by hand and holds.
scenarios.off-base: The machine R-2 is about: one name of every origin class beside the names the distribution's own repositories serve. On apt, a package from o=Docker, one from a PPA (o=LP-PPA-...), one whose installed version's only source is /var/lib/dpkg/status, one from o=Debian a=bookworm-backports, and one from the release's own suite. On pacman, a name chaotic-aur alone offers, one extra offers, one both offer, and one pacman -Qqem reports. Only the base-origin names are declared; the rest are named under their classes.
scenarios.off-index: The machine that has never fetched an index: every source line `apt-cache policy` prints for it is /var/lib/dpkg/status, and the no-argument listing names that source alone. It is the off-base machine's own package set under that one difference, so the pair proves what the index decides: with it, three of the five chosen names are left out; without it, all five are declared as read and the import warns once with W_UNCHECKED_ORIGIN. A Debian 12 cloud image really is this machine until apt-get update has run on it, which is how R-2 found the case (LD-316). There is no pacman recording of it: the harness writes a sync database into every scratch root, and the pacman backend reads that directory rather than an -Si answer, so tests/host_pacman.rs proves that half directly.
scenarios.sources: The chosen machine with Docker's repository enabled in deb822 form and installed from (containerd.io automatic, docker-ce and docker-ce-cli chosen), plus a root/ subtree the test copies into the scratch root: /etc/apt/sources.list with the distribution's own three stanzas, an enabled repository nothing installed came from, a plain-http .list, a vendor .list with one [trusted=yes] line and one unsigned line, an empty credential file under /etc/apt/auth.conf.d/, and Packages index files under /var/lib/apt/lists that the import no longer reads (LD-367). Its policy.txt is the chosen machine's with Docker's source rows added, and its policy-release.txt names every source those stanzas list, the distribution's with o=Debian and the others with invented origins, so the Docker names are off-base under R-2 and attributed, by apt-cache policy alone, to the commented [sources.docker] block. Every URI is invented (.invalid) except Docker's public one; docker.asc is a generated ASCII-armor public block and idle.gpg one generated public-key packet, framing only and not keys.
scenarios.mirror: The sources machine served by a country mirror of the distribution: /etc/apt/sources.list names an invented plain-http mirror outside *.debian.org whose release rows say o=Debian, and Docker's stanza carries Architectures. The mirror's stanzas are the distribution's own and are counted, never refused; Docker's block is carried with architectures in its place (LD-367).
scenarios.compressed: The sources machine whose apt keeps its indexes compressed (Acquire::GzipIndexes): /var/lib/apt/lists holds only generated .lz4 files and no plain Packages index. Attribution reads apt-cache policy alone, so Docker's packages are still attributed and its block carried (LD-367).
scenarios.ambiguous: The sources machine with a second repository, docker-mirror.sources, whose recorded source row offers the very version of docker-ce that is installed: docker-ce is offered by two repositories and attributed to neither (NOT CAPTURED, ambiguous); docker-ce-cli, offered by Docker's alone, is still Docker's, and the second repository, with nothing attributed to it alone, is refused by name (LD-367).
scenarios.ambiguous-multi-uri: The ambiguous machine with its two repositories in one deb822 stanza: docker.sources lists Docker's URI and the mirror's in one URIs field, and no second file exists. docker-ce's installed version is offered by both repositories, so it is ambiguous under NOT CAPTURED and in no block, although one stanza lists both; docker-ce-cli, offered by Docker's alone, is carried in that stanza's block (si-1 validator-repair-1, LD-367).
scenarios.ambiguous-unlisted: The ambiguous machine without docker-mirror.sources: apt-cache policy still offers docker-ce's installed version from Docker's repository, which docker.sources lists, and from the mirror, which no stanza of the files lodi reads lists. docker-ce is ambiguous under NOT CAPTURED and in no block, never attributed to the one listed repository; docker-ce-cli, offered by Docker's alone, is carried (si-1 validator-repair-1, LD-367).
scenarios.own-suite: The Debian 12 chosen machine with /etc/apt/sources.list.d/debian.sources writing every suite by its alias, as a Debian 12 machine may since Debian 13 became stable: one stanza lists oldstable, oldstable-updates and oldstable-proposed-updates, the other oldstable-security. Its policy.txt is the chosen machine's with the source rows under oldstable, and its policy-release.txt gives each suite's release fields with o=Debian and the codename form in n= (bookworm, bookworm-updates, bookworm-proposed-updates, bookworm-security). The aliases of the three default suites are counted; oldstable-proposed-updates, which a fresh install does not enable, is named under NOT CAPTURED by the file that lists it, and that stanza is still counted (LD-414).
scenarios.mixed-backports: The Debian 12 own-suite recording with oldstable-backports (n=bookworm-backports, o=Debian Backports) beside the default oldstable and oldstable-updates in one deb822 stanza. The default suites are counted and the extra suite is named by its file even when no package was installed from it (LD-414, R8).
scenarios.one-line-proposed: The Ubuntu 24.04 proposed recording with two lines in one ubuntu-proposed.list, deb and deb-src, naming the same noble-proposed suite. The import names that suite once by its file rather than repeating the refusal (LD-414, R8).
scenarios.proposed: The Ubuntu 24.04 chosen machine with the image's own /etc/apt/sources.list.d/ubuntu.sources (noble, noble-updates and noble-backports; noble-security) and noble-proposed enabled in ubuntu-proposed.sources, a stanza of its own, as Ubuntu documents enabling it. Its policy-release.txt gives every suite those stanzas list with o=Ubuntu. The two default stanzas are counted; noble-proposed is named under NOT CAPTURED by its file, with why lodi does not write it (LD-414).
scenarios.unattributed: The sources machine after Docker's repository was removed: no stanza and no keyring for it, and apt-cache policy offers docker-ce and docker-ce-cli from /var/lib/dpkg/status alone. With lodi-hand-built they are attributed to no block and named under NOT CAPTURED as unattributed, never guessed (LD-367).

files.os-release: The identity the safety gate reads, per distribution.
files.dpkg-query.txt: dpkg-query -W of name, version and status.
files.dpkg-survey.txt: dpkg-query -W of name, status, Priority, Section, Depends and Recommends.
files.policy.txt: apt-cache policy NAME...: the installed and candidate versions and the version table, whose source rows are what R-2 classifies the installed version by. Every source row's text is the key the no-argument listing states that source's release fields under.
files.pacman-Q.txt: Every installed package with its version.
files.pacman-Qi.txt: Name, Version and Depends On per installed package.
files.pacman-Qqem.txt: The foreign names: installed from no repository pacman knows. An empty recording means what a real Arch guest does when there is no such package: it prints nothing and exits 1 (observed 2026-09-22 by M-Import T-5; LD-301).
files.pacman-Si.txt: The candidates the sync databases offer.
files.pacman-Si.err: What pacman prints on stderr for a name no repository has, replayed with a non-zero exit.
files.snaps.txt: One snap file name per line; the test creates them under var/lib/snapd/snaps in its scratch root.
files.flatpaks.txt: One flatpak application id per line; the test creates them under var/lib/flatpak/app in its scratch root.
files.expected.toml: The host.toml the emitter must produce for that scenario, byte for byte. Regenerate with LODI_RECORD_EXPECTED=1 and review the diff; no validation command sets it.
files.conffiles.txt: dpkg-query -W -f=${Conffiles}: one "/path md5" pair per line per package, with dpkg's obsolete marker on the rows that carry it. The test replays it; the apt backend digests the file in the scratch root to decide whether it is changed. An empty recording is a machine whose packages report no conffile.
files.pacman-Qii.txt: pacman -Qii: the Backup Files field, where pacman prints its own verdict beside each path it tracks, as "/etc/nanorc [modified]". The arch/capture recording was corrected to this layout on 2026-09-22, from a pacman 7 guest read by M-Import T-5; the hand-authored shape it replaced put the verdict first and no pacman prints it that way, so the core read nothing at all from a real machine (docs/DISCREPANCIES.md, LD-302).
files.dpkg-query-binary.txt: dpkg-query -W of name, version and status as ${binary:Package} prints it: architecture-qualified for every Multi-Arch package. Only the multiarch scenario records one; a scenario without this file models a machine where the two spellings are the same text, and its shim falls back to the plain recording.
files.dpkg-survey-binary.txt: The survey reading as ${binary:Package} prints it, beside dpkg-survey.txt, for the same reason.
files.policy-release.txt: apt-cache policy with no argument: the release fields (o=, l=, a=, c=) of every enabled source. It is the only reading that tells a Docker or a PPA source from the distribution's own. Its origin lines are host names and the product never reads them.
files.pacman-conf-repo-list.txt: pacman-conf --repo-list: the repositories this machine has enabled, one per line. A scenario without this file models a machine with no pacman-conf, where the shim exits 1 and the family's own repository names decide alone.
files.root/: A subtree copied into the scratch root before the import reads it: the apt source lists, keyrings and index files a machine has. Only the sources scenario carries one.

real_readings: M-Import T-5 takes readings off fresh guests and records them. These hand-authored recordings are what the import core is proved against offline, and a shape they get wrong is a shape the core gets wrong: the guest runs of T-5 corrected two of them, and each correction is named beside the file it changed.
